headline: Attackers are using Google search ads that pass through Bing's trusted web address to send Mac users to a fake Claude download that tricks them into running a hidden command.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a clever ad-abuse scam using an AI brand, but one campaign, payload unknown and no victim numbers reported.
importance_line: Mac users who search for AI tools can be sent to a convincing fake by a paid ad that looks legitimate, but the final malware is unknown and no victim numbers are reported.
summary: BleepingComputer reports, citing security firm Push Security, that attackers placed Google search ads for "claude mac" that route through bing.com and a hacked website to a fake Claude download page, where the copy button for the install command secretly swaps in a different command that fetches and runs a remote script. Push Security calls the technique "Adception" and says it delivers a ClickFix attack, which tricks users into running a harmful command themselves; what malware, if any, the script installs is not known.
notes: Push Security report not read; relayed by BleepingComputer.
